feed.description: Conversas sobre construção de trilhas: drenagem, traçado, e as pessoas que constroem o caminho. Contraparte portuguesa de Singletrack Sessions.
feed.title: Sessões de Trilha

bullets: Drainage is the design decision that has the biggest impact on any trail's longevity—ignoring it leads to reconstruction within a year.
Excavating with too steep a slope is the most common mistake new builders make, causing long-term erosion and structural failure.
Cuts in the benching (or berm) on slopes are not optional—shortcuts taken in the first year result in collapse by the third year.
Soil structure is more important than people realize, and its failure mode is often invisible until after the first rainy season.
Land management discussions must happen before the first excavation, as they define the commitments being made to the environment.
The structure of the team is more important than individuals, and teams using the Cascadia Alliance framework show repeatable success patterns.
Machine-made trails are not inherently worse than hand-made ones—understanding this shift enables better decision-making across all scales.
Outside of proven tools like RockShox or Spoke & Wrench, detecting failure modes becomes significantly harder, leading to costly rework.
